claims.claim: Baur calls the Forgotten Realms the kitchen sink approach to world building.
claims.source: Wolfgang Baur, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 1, 2025
claims.quote: The Forgotten Realms is the kitchen sink approach to world building

claims.claim: Baur describes a newer one-book model as providing the minimum viable world building.
claims.source: Wolfgang Baur, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 1, 2025
claims.quote: to provide the minimum viable world building
claims.page: exchange on models of world building

claims.claim: Cook says the worst world building books he has read are literally just lists of places and people.
claims.source: David 'Zeb' Cook, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 2, 2025
claims.quote: are ones that are literally just lists of places and people

claims.claim: Cook faults such books for never saying that one town hates the town next to it.
claims.source: David 'Zeb' Cook, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 2, 2025
claims.quote: this town hates this town over here

claims.claim: Cook says a published world is not created for yourself but for other players to take and use.
claims.source: David 'Zeb' Cook, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 2, 2025
claims.quote: You are not creating a world for yourself

claims.claim: Richard Green says a new setting book must make clear at once what kind of adventures take place in that world.
claims.source: Richard Green, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 2, 2025
claims.quote: needs to be super clear what kind of adventures take place

claims.claim: Baur says the expected arc of play should be stated explicitly to players rather than kept coy.
claims.source: Wolfgang Baur, Kobold Press world building seminar transcript, part 2, 2025
claims.quote: you should be explicit about it. Don’t be coy

claims.claim: Baur's opening essay describes good campaign setting design as stacking as many boxes of dynamite as possible.
claims.source: Wolfgang Baur, Kobold Guide to Worldbuilding p.12, quoted in a Gnome Stew review
claims.quote: to stack as many boxes of dynamite as possible

claims.claim: The reviewer reads the Kobold Guide as telling setting designers they need not create all the details necessary for play.
claims.source: Gnome Stew review of the Kobold Guide to Worldbuilding
claims.quote: we don’t have to create all of the details necessary

claims.claim: The reviewer says the book advises leaving the finer mechanics to the GMs and players who pick up the work.
claims.source: Gnome Stew review of the Kobold Guide to Worldbuilding
claims.quote: it is better to leave the finer mechanics to the GMs and players

claims.claim: Mizer reports that Carbonell conceptualises tabletop role-playing games first and foremost as literary gametexts.
claims.source: Nicholas J. Mizer, 'The Role of the Cosmographer', International Journal of Role-playing 18, 2025
claims.quote: conceptualizing TRPGs as, first and foremost, “literary gametexts”

claims.claim: Mizer argues the role-playing game emerges as a set of practices only later codified in a gametext.
claims.source: Nicholas J. Mizer, 'The Role of the Cosmographer', International Journal of Role-playing 18, 2025
claims.quote: a set of practices which are only later codified

claims.claim: Mizer holds that a cosmographer is not so much a worldbuilder as a world-hopper.
claims.source: Nicholas J. Mizer, 'The Role of the Cosmographer', International Journal of Role-playing 18, 2025
claims.quote: so much a worldbuilder as a world-hopper

claims.claim: A reviewer says Dread Trident theorises the posthuman by centering the gametexts and gametools that create gameplay.
claims.source: Adrianna Burton, 'Book Review: Dread Trident', Analog Game Studies, 2022
claims.quote: centering the gametexts and gametools that create gameplay

claims.feature: other: close reading of game texts
claims.claim: The reviewer says Carbonell answers his question through a series of close readings of several TRPGs.
claims.source: Adrianna Burton, 'Book Review: Dread Trident', Analog Game Studies, 2022
claims.quote: through a series of close readings of several TRPGs
